intended_object: The naive locus of a homomorphism u : A →* E(H), for a finite group A, viewed as an open subscheme of H. Here E is an elliptic curve over S and H is an S-scheme. The naive locus is the set of points h of H where u is injective on the fibre, meaning that for every a ≠ 1 the section u(a) does not meet the zero section at h. This is taken from the docstring and the module documentation, which cite Katz–Mazur §3.7.
explanation: The definition just packages the set `naiveLocus u` with the proof `isOpen_naiveLocus` that it is open, giving an element of `H.left.Opens`, which is Mathlib's type of open subschemes. The underlying set is defined as {h | ∀ a ≠ 1, (u a).left h ≠ E.zero (H.hom h)}. Both points lie over the same point H.hom h of S, and the zero section is a section of the structure map. So the condition says exactly that u(a)(h) is not in the image of the zero section. Over κ(h) this means the restriction of u(a) to the fibre is not the identity, so the condition is fibrewise injectivity of u at h. Finiteness of A is the hypothesis that makes this set open: it is a finite intersection of complements of preimages of the closed image of the zero section. So the hypothesis belongs to the construction and is not a narrowing. Mathlib has no general version of this notion, since it is specific to group schemes and elliptic curves.
